name: Montreal
editorial_article: "Montreal" is a haunting, atmospheric R&B track by Canadian singer-songwriter The Weeknd, originally released as part of his 2011 mixtape 'Echoes of Silence'. Produced by The Weeknd alongside his frequent collaborator Illangelo, the song stands as a seminal entry in the "Alternative R&B" movement that defined the early 2010s. Known for its dark, brooding soundscape—driven by thunderous bass, rattling snares, and The Weeknd's signature soaring, melancholic falsetto—the track explores themes of emotional detachment, loneliness, and the casual brutality of transient relationships. \n\nOne of the most distinct features of "Montreal" is its creative use of sampling; the track prominently features a vocal loop from France Gall's 1964 song "Laisse Tomber les Filles." By repurposing this retro French pop sample, The Weeknd and Illangelo create a jarring, surreal contrast against the song’s modern, dark-pop production, underscoring the lyrical themes of heartbreak and apathy. "Montreal" captures the essence of the "trilogy" era of the artist’s discography, helping to solidify his reputation for crafting cold, nocturnal music that resonated deeply with a generation disillusioned by modern romance. It remains a fan favorite and a critical point of analysis for those studying the evolution of contemporary R&B, illustrating how the artist seamlessly blended mainstream pop sensibilities with an unconventional, underground aesthetic. The song later appeared on the 2012 compilation album 'Trilogy', which served to introduce these underground mixtapes to a much wider international audience.
